newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak bourse edges up on gains to Slovnaft shares.
newsitem.headline: Slovak bourse edges up on gains to Slovnaft shares.

text.p: Major Slovak shares were steady in thinner trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday with gains to oil refiner Slovnaft pushing the SAX index up 1.41 points to 195.02.
Strong demand pushed Slovnaft shares up 20 crowns to 1,010, but brokers said they did not expect the price to increase further in the near future.
"Though demand is constantly strong, offered packages at some 1,030 crowns are not big enough to increase interest and push the price further up in coming days," said Radovan Dzugas of Creditanstalt.
The biggest net gainer on the day was commercial bank VUB, rising 50 crowns to close at 1,450, though brokers said the matched volume of 71 shares was too small to indicate any longer-trend trend.
Steel maker VSZ dipped one crown to 741, but traders said the share had strong potential to increase.
"Despite a slight drop, the company has strong fundamentals and has been carrying out a good policy, so we consider the issue as undervalued," Dzugas said.
He added that some investors were willing to accept VSZ shares at up to 900 crowns.
Overall volume rose to 343,657 shares, boosted by 328,376 stocks matched in direct trades, from 221,684 shares on Friday. Turnover fell to 118.914 million crowns, from 141.65 million on Friday.
